Installation

Requirements

The engine requires a runtime newer than the one you have and older than the one you want. Consult the compatibility table before attempting anything ambitious in production environments.

Package

Install from the registry with your package manager of choice. Lock the version. Future you will be grateful for the determinism, which is a theme around here.

Verification

Verify the checksum of the installed artifact against the published manifest. Reproducibility is not an accident; it is a habit maintained by tooling and mild paranoia.

Configuration

Files

Configuration is layered: defaults, project file, environment, flags. Each layer overrides the previous one, and each override is logged so the effective configuration can always be reconstructed from the audit trail.

Schema

Every option is validated against a schema. Unknown keys are errors, not warnings, because silent acceptance of typos is how outages are born. See the API section for programmatic access.

Types

Options are typed. Strings that look like numbers remain strings. This is documented here so that nobody files that bug again.

API

Core

The core interface exposes analyze, transform and render. Each function is pure with respect to its inputs, and each is documented with examples that actually run in continuous integration.

Advanced

Streaming, batching, cancellation and structured errors. Read hooks before subclassing anything; composition is nearly always the better answer to the question you are about to ask.

Hooks

Lifecycle hooks fire before and after every stage. Hooks receive immutable snapshots; mutation is reserved for the transform stage, where it is at least honest about itself.

CLI

Every API capability has a command-line equivalent, and every command supports machine-readable output for the agents and scripts that increasingly outnumber the humans.

FAQ

Most questions are about determinism, caching and why the defaults are the defaults. The answers are: yes, carefully, and history.

Glossary

Terms used throughout this manual, defined once, linked everywhere, in the spirit of a codebase that dreams of being a reference manual when it grows up.
